raw_text:
Below is a single, concise but detailed 12‑week postpartum return‑to‑exercise, strength, core and cardio plan plus breastfeeding nutrition and recovery guidance for your 33‑year‑old client who is 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section. It assumes OB clearance to walk now and to resume broader activity at the 6‑week check. Progress only when symptoms are absent (no pelvic pressure/heaviness, no new urinary/fecal leakage, no incision pain, no midline bulging/doming). Recommend pelvic‑floor physiotherapy screen when possible.

High‑level timeline
- Weeks 1–2 (postpartum weeks 4–6): Healing & gentle movement. Walking, breathing/pelvic‑floor reconnection, light bodyweight activation. No abdominal loading.
- Weeks 3–4 (postpartum weeks 6–8): OB cleared for broader activity. Start light strength, pelvic‑floor reconnection, increase walking. Start very gentle core reconnection.
- Weeks 5–6 (postpartum weeks 8–10): Increase strength volume and tempo control; introduce light household loading; progress cardio intervals (walk/jog or power‑walk).
- Weeks 7–9 (postpartum weeks 10–13) — Phase 3 (deliberate intensity push): Higher intensity strength (RPE 6–8), heavier functional loads, carries, higher‑intensity intervals. Start cautious HIIT (low‑impact first) if cleared and tolerated.
- Weeks 10–12 (postpartum weeks 13–16): Consolidate strength and cardio gains, progress to near pre‑pregnancy training patterns; return to more intense cardio/HIIT only if pelvic floor, incision, and core tolerance are good.

Weekly structure (throughout)
- Strength: 3 sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri). Session length increases from ~20 min to ~45 min by later weeks.
- Cardio: daily walks + 2 structured cardio sessions/week starting week 6, progressing to 3 sessions/week in Phase 3; HIIT introduced cautiously from ~week 10 if tolerated earlier.
- Core/pelvic floor: daily gentle breathing/awareness early; targeted core sessions 3×/week from week 6 onward with staged progressions.
- Recovery: 1–2 active recovery days/week (mobility, gentle walks); prioritise sleep, nutrition, hydration.

Safety & progression checkpoints (stop/regress and refer if any of the following)
- New/increased urinary or fecal leakage, urgency, or pelvic heaviness/pressure.
- Visible bulging/doming of the midline during/after exercise.
- Incision pain, increased bleeding, fever, or dizziness.
- Persistent or increasing fatigue, or drop in milk supply after increased activity.

Phase by phase — week‑by‑week summary

Weeks 1–2 (Postpartum weeks 4–6) — Healing & gentle reconnection
- Goals: promote circulation, gentle pelvic‑floor awareness; rebuild gentle strength and posture.
- Daily: walks 10–20 min (1–2×), diaphragmatic breathing and very gentle pelvic‑floor draws (3–5 min, 2×/day), daily mobility 8–12 min.
- Strength (3×/week; 20 min):
  - Glute bridges 2x8–10
  - Wall push‑ups 2x6–8
  - Standing hip abductions 2x10/side
  - Heel slides or seated knee extensions 2x8/side
  - Scapular squeezes 2x12
- Nutrition: +300 kcal/day conservative start for breastfeeding, protein ~20–30 g per meal, hydrate 2.5–3 L/day, continue prenatal/multivitamin.

Weeks 3–4 (Postpartum weeks 6–8) — Gentle strength & core reconnection (start after 6‑week OB clearance)
- Goals: build pelvic‑floor coordination, low‑load strength, increase walking.
- Daily: walks 20–35 min; diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic‑floor holds (gentle 3–5s holds × 4–6 × 2/day); mobility 10 min.
- Strength (3×/week; 25–35 min)
  Session A (lower focus): Glute bridge 3x10–12; supported split squat 3x8/leg; calf raises 3x12; bird‑dog 2x6–8/side; clamshells 2x12/side.
  Session B (upper focus): Incline push‑ups 3x8–10; table rows 3x10–12; light overhead press 2x10; scapular wall slides 2x12.
  Session C (full body): Circuit x3: 10 sit‑to‑stand, 10 glute bridges, 8 assisted lunges/leg, 10 rows.
- Core: start very gentle TA draw, heel‑slides with cueing; no crunches/planks.
- Cardio: brisk walks and optional hill walks; still no jogging unless cleared and tolerated.
- Nutrition: emphasise protein after workouts, iron and iodine sources.

Weeks 5–6 (Postpartum weeks 8–10) — Build load tolerance & volume
- Goals: increase training volume, start light external load (household items), build steady cardio base.
- Daily: walks 30–45 min most days; pelvic‑floor holds 3×6–8; mobility/scar care if healed.
- Strength (3×/week; 30–40 min)
  Session A (lower): Bulgarian/split squats 3–4x8; single‑leg RDL 3x8/side; glute bridge variations 3x8–12; calf raises 3x12.
  Session B (upper): Incline→knee push‑ups 3–4x8–12; one‑arm rows 3x8–10; overhead press 3x10; reverse fly 2x12.
  Session C (functional): Circuit x4: 12 squats to chair (3s down), 10 step‑ups each, 12 bridges, 10 rows.
- Cardio: Walk intervals and steady brisk walks; optional short jog/walk test if no pelvic symptoms (very conservative).
- Nutrition: increase carbs modestly around workouts; protein snack post‑session.

Weeks 7–9 (Postpartum weeks 10–13) — Phase 3: deliberate intensity push (target strong by week 12)
- Goals: reach higher intensity strength (RPE 6–8), heavier functional loads, interval cardio and cautious HIIT introduction (low‑impact first); begin stronger core work.
- Frequency: Strength 3×/week (lower, upper, full), Cardio 3×/week (intervals + circuits + long walk), daily walks.
- Strength sessions (~40–50 min) example:
  Day 1 Lower (heavy focus): Bulgarian split squat 4x6–8 (increase loading weekly), single‑leg RDL 4x6–8, loaded hip thrust 4x8–10, weighted step‑ups 3x8–10, dead bug 3x10/side.
  Day 2 Upper (push/pull): Progress push‑ups (incline → knee → negatives) 4x6–10, one‑arm rows 4x6–8, overhead press 4x8–10, accessory 3x10–12.
  Day 3 Full body & carries: Circuit 4 rounds (goblet‑style squats, reverse lunges, rows, bridges); farmer/suitcase carries 3×40–60m; short power drill (intent, low amplitude) if tolerated.
- Cardio:
  - Interval run/walk or power‑walk intervals (30 min): 5 warm, 6–8×(1 min jog/2 min walk) or power walk alternative. Progress work:rest each week.
  - Cardio strength circuit (low impact) 30–35 min.
  - Long brisk walk 40–60 min.
- HIIT: introduce 1 low‑impact HIIT session/week if all prior sessions tolerated—e.g., 20 min: 8×(30s hard / 60s easy) of non‑impact moves. Add more only if symptom‑free.
- Core: progress to dead bug variations, bird‑dog, standing anti‑rotation, short side planks on knees → feet only if no doming and pelvic‑floor OK.
- Progression plan across 3 weeks: increase load, decrease rest, increase interval intensity/volume moderately so she feels measurably stronger by end of the phase (week 12).

Weeks 10–12 (Postpartum weeks 13–16) — Consolidation & return toward pre‑pregnancy training
- Goals: solidify strength and cardio gains; introduce higher demand core and more HIIT/impact only if cleared and symptom‑free.
- Strength (3×/week; 40–50 min):
  - Heavier unilateral work: Bulgarian split squat 4x6–8 heavier; single‑leg RDL 4x8; hip thrust 4x8–10 with load; push‑ups progression 4x6–12; rows 4x8–10; overhead press 3x8–10.
  - Core: full plank progressions, dead bug advanced, Pallof presses, farmer carries for anti‑rotation.
- Cardio:
  - Can include 1–2 higher intensity sessions/week (HIIT allowed if pelvic floor and incision ok), one tempo session, one long steady state walk/run.

HIIT summary (when and how)
- Earliest introduction: after 8–10 weeks and only if no pelvic‑floor symptoms and strength & low‑impact intervals were well tolerated. More conservative: wait until 12+ weeks.

- New/increasing pelvic heaviness or pressure, urinary/fecal leakage, inability to control midline bulge, incision pain or signs of infection, dizziness, syncope, increased bleeding.

- Prioritise form over load and progress in small increments (10% rule).
